name: Seahawks
subhead: 2026 training camp edition — defending Super Bowl LX champions, a fifth offensive coordinator in five years for Sam Darnold, and HBO cameras in the building.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Champions. Seattle beat New England 29–13 in Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium after a 14–3 regular season, then dispatched San Francisco 41–6 and the Rams 31–27 to get there.

New play-caller, familiar scheme. Rookie offensive coordinator Brian Fleury takes over — Darnold's fifth OC in five years — but is installing a system similar to Kubiak's, with new position coaches Jake Peetz and Tyson Prince alongside him.
Schneider's draft posture: the GM said openly the champions wanted to trade down — "it's no secret with us" — prioritizing volume over a single high pick.
Hard Knocks. A five-episode season debuts Aug. 4, featuring Macdonald, Darnold, 2025 Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Devon Witherspoon and Byron Murphy II.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: Re-signedRashid Shaheed, WR — three years, up to $51M. Seattle had acquired him in one of the biggest deals of the 2025 trade deadline; keeping him was the offseason's clearest priority.
SignedOLB Dante Fowler Jr. to bolster the edge rotation.
LostKenneth Walker III, RB — the Super Bowl MVP — departed in free agency, the most striking exit of any champion's offseason.
LostEDGE Boye Mafe, CB Riq Woolen (to Philadelphia) and S Coby Bryant (to Chicago) all found new homes.
Continuity where it counted: Darnold, Smith-Njigba, Witherspoon and Murphy II all return as the spine of the roster.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Sam Darnold, QB. From first-round pick to journeyman backup to Pro Bowler to Super Bowl champion. The uncomfortable footnote: he led the NFL in turnovers during the regular season before playing clean football in the playoffs. Coaxing better decisions out of him is the coaching staff's stated task.
The OC carousel. Fleury is Darnold's fifth coordinator in five years. Scheme continuity with Kubiak's system is the mitigating factor.

Tory Horton, WR. The single biggest swing factor on offense. He caught five touchdowns in his first eight games as a rookie, then lost the rest of the season to a shin injury. Health decides how explosive this offense is.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR. The reigning Offensive Player of the Year and the offense's non-negotiable.
Running back, wide open. Walker's departure leaves the Super Bowl MVP's carries unclaimed.
Secondary, reshuffled. Woolen and Bryant both left; Witherspoon and Murphy II now carry more.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Super Bowl MVP departed in free agency

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Seattle won a title and then watched its Super Bowl MVP running back, two starting defensive backs and an edge rusher walk out the door — the ordinary tax of a championship cap sheet. What stayed is the part that matters most: Macdonald's defense, Smith-Njigba, and a quarterback who finally has proof to point at. The repeat case rests on two things nobody can schedule — Tory Horton staying upright, and Darnold carrying his January decision-making into September.
